title: Preserve the controlled relation source fact key (customerId) through computed-column projection and hidden-dependency stripping so relation cells resolve instead of showing 'missing'
description: Stage-1 genuine functional defect confirmed by the newest browser acceptance (.ai/logs/report-stage1-browser-formula-relation-20261004.json, stage_complete=false) and verified in source. When a report definition combines controlled relations (customer.code/customer.country) with computed columns OR with composite grouping/pivot, the hidden relation source fact key customerId is stripped from preview rows BEFORE ReportConfigurationRelationResolver.EnrichAsync runs, so ReadCustomerId returns null and relation cells resolve to 'missing' even for an existing, in-scope customer. Two independent stripping sites cause this: (1) ReportConfigurationComputedProjection.Apply projects each row from definition.Fields + computed-column keys only (it is invoked with definition.Fields, not the BuildFields output that includes customerId), dropping customerId whenever computed columns are present with groupBy=none; (2) ReportConfigurationExecutionService.ExecutePreviewAsync / ExecuteMatchedSetPreviewAsync call StripCompositeDependencies (and ApplyMetrics) before ApplyRelationsAsync, so composite grouping (>=2 base dimensions) or pivot also removes customerId before relation enrichment. The resolver already strips customerId afterward via StripHiddenSourceKey when it is not a selected field, so the fix is to preserve customerId through projection and reorder relation enrichment before hidden-dependency stripping, then let the resolver strip it. No schema, SQL, secrets, permission, or production change; only the two source files plus regression tests.
acceptance_criteria: When a sales-order or receivable report definition combines controlled relations with computed columns, the computed-column projection preserves the relation source fact key (customerId) in each projected row so relation cells resolve to the authorized customer code/country (not 'missing'); the hidden customerId is stripped from the final preview rows and columns and never leaked.

When a report definition combines controlled relations with composite grouping (two base dimensions) or a pivot, relation enrichment runs before hidden-dependency stripping in both the current-page and matched-set execution paths, so relation cells resolve correctly and the hidden source key is stripped afterward; missing/deleted/forbidden cell semantics are preserved.

Add executable regression tests (sales-order, and receivable via the shared projection helper) covering relations combined with computed columns and with composite grouping, asserting nonempty resolved relation values, correct missing/deleted/forbidden cell reasons, and that customerId never appears in final rows/columns; run safe Release build and ERP.UnitTests without regressing existing relation/computed/grouping tests.
implementation_evidence: src/ERP.Infrastructure/Reports/ReportConfigurationDatasetProvider.cs:158 (SalesOrder BuildFields adds customerId to the FETCH list when relations exist, but :194-195 passes definition.Fields — not BuildFields output — into ReportConfigurationComputedProjection.Apply, and :1625-1703 projects only selected fields + computed-column keys, dropping customerId); Receivable provider mirrors this at :931-932 with BuildFields at :1023-1025; src/ERP.Application/Services/ReportConfigurationExecutionService.cs:370-373 (current-page) and :447-450 (matched-set) run ApplyMetrics then StripCompositeDependencies (which at :560-586 removes any non-selected key incl. customerId when Groupings.Count>=2 or Pivot!=null) BEFORE ApplyRelationsAsync (:373/:450 -> :588-600 -> RelationResolver.EnrichAsync); src/ERP.Infrastructure/Reports/ReportConfigurationRelationResolver.cs:132-142 ReadCustomerId returns null when customerId was already stripped, yielding the '缺失/missing' reason at :163-164. Live proof: .ai/logs/report-stage1-browser-formula-relation-20261004.json relation_issue { customer.code: missing, customer.country: missing } with cause 'ComputedProjection strips hidden customerId before RelationResolver ... Requires functional repair'. Existing relation unit tests (ReportConfigurationRelationTests.cs:319-356) cover relations WITHOUT computed columns so they never exercise this path.
